subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Trillion Tree Debate
description: A 60-second lesson on The Trillion Tree Debate.

hook.text: A 2019 study said planting a trillion trees could capture two-thirds of human emissions.

buildup.text: The idea went viral. Governments and corporations pledged billions of trees.

discovery.text: Critics quickly pointed out the math was flawed — the real capture is much lower.

twist.text: Planting trees on grasslands and savannas can actually harm those ecosystems.

climax.text: Planting the right trees in the right places helps. Planting anywhere just for numbers hurts.

punchline.text: A trillion trees is a slogan. Where they go is what matters.

quiz.question: Why did scientists criticize the trillion-tree campaign?
options: The carbon capture math was overestimated
Trees were too expensive to plant

details.summary: A 2019 study claimed planting a trillion trees could capture 200 billion tons of carbon, sparking global excitement and criticism. Scientists objected that the study overestimated potential, underestimated challenges, and risked distracting from the priority of cutting emissions.
details.whyItMatters: The trillion-tree debate highlights both the promise and the limits of tree planting as a climate solution. Trees help, but they are not a substitute for decarbonization.
takeaways: The original trillion-tree estimate has been significantly revised downward
Planting on natural grasslands and savannas can harm ecosystems
Protecting existing forests stores carbon faster than planting new ones

faq.question: Can planting a trillion trees solve climate change?
faq.answer: No. Even optimistic estimates suggest tree planting could offset only a fraction of annual emissions. Trees take decades to mature, are vulnerable to fire and drought, and cannot substitute for the urgent need to stop burning fossil fuels.

faq.question: Why is planting trees on grasslands harmful?
faq.answer: Natural grasslands and savannas are biodiverse ecosystems adapted to fire and grazing. Planting trees on them destroys native habitat, reduces water availability, and can actually decrease soil carbon in some grassland types.
